name: Jester
description: A fast notepad for Windows, in purple and gold. One portable file: download it and start typing.

hero.lede: A fast notepad for Windows, in purple and gold. One portable file: download it and start typing.
notes: If Windows says it protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway.
hero.away: Jester runs on Windows. Open this page on your PC to download it.

image.name: hero
image.alt: Jester with five tabs open, a C# file in the editor with line numbers and the status bar showing line, column and encoding

features.label: Tabs
features.title: Unsaved tabs survive a restart
body: Close Jester with unsaved or Untitled tabs and they come back with their text on the next start, marked with an asterisk.
The session is written as you type, so a crash or a shutdown keeps them too.

main.name: f5
main.alt: Jester after a restart with the unsaved Untitled and recipe tabs back

features.label: Replace
features.title: Find and replace in one dialog
body: Find Next, Replace and Replace All, with match case, wrap around and a search direction. Replace All is one step that Undo takes back.

main.name: f1
main.alt: The Replace dialog over a recipe, replacing sugar with honey

features.label: Search
features.title: Search a whole folder at once
body: Find in Files, Ctrl+Shift+F, searches a folder and its subfolders, with filters such as *.cs. Double-click a result to open the file at that line.

main.name: f2
main.alt: Find in Files results: nine matches in three files

features.label: Encodings
features.title: Every file keeps its encoding
body: Files open in the encoding they were saved in and are written back the same way, line endings included.
If a file still looks wrong, File, Reopen with Encoding reads it again in the encoding you pick.

main.name: f3
main.alt: The File menu with Reopen with Encoding open on a Windows-1252 file

features.label: Format
features.title: Line endings in one click
body: The Format menu switches a tab between Windows, Unix and old Mac line endings, and between UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM and UTF-16. Word wrap, auto indent and the font sit in the same menu.

main.name: f4
main.alt: The Format menu with Line Endings open and Windows (CRLF) ticked

The Replace dialog always shows all of its options.

requirements: No install and no admin rights

privacy.title: No network at all
body: Jester has no network code and sends nothing anywhere. The only other program it starts is your PDF viewer, and only if you say yes after exporting a PDF.

data.title: One folder, nothing next to the exe
body: Your settings, open tabs and the text of unsaved tabs live in %APPDATA%\Jester. Settings are saved a moment after each change, and the session as you type.

basics.title: Get started
steps: Double-click it. There is nothing to install.

basics.title: Updates
body: Download the new Jester.exe and put it in place of the old one. Your settings and tabs stay, because they live in %APPDATA%\Jester.

basics.title: Removing it
body: Close every Jester window, then delete Jester.exe and the %APPDATA%\Jester folder. Save unsaved tabs first; their text lives in that folder.

a: Yes. Jester is free software under the GNU GPL v3.0.

faq.q: Why does Windows say it protected my PC?
a: Jester is not signed with a paid certificate, so Windows warns about it the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.

faq.q: Do I have to install anything?
a: No. Jester.exe is one portable file with everything it needs inside. Double-click it, no admin rights needed.

faq.q: Where does Jester keep my data?
a: In %APPDATA%\Jester: settings.json for your preferences and window, sessions for your open tabs, and crash.log only if something went wrong. Nothing is written next to the exe.

faq.q: What happens to unsaved tabs if I close Jester or it crashes?
a: They come back with their text the next time you start it. Jester keeps unsaved and Untitled tabs as you type, so closing never asks you to save them.

closing.title: Get Jester
closing.sub: Free for Windows 10 and 11. One file, nothing to install.
